findings.problem: SessionWorkflow uses redundant boolean flags (status: String, is_validated: bool, is_sent: bool) instead of an enum or typestate, making it possible to represent invalid states such as is_sent=true with status="pending" or sent_at_epoch_ms=None
findings.failure_mode: Domain invariants cannot be enforced by the type system; callers can read inconsistent state without any runtime check, leading to silent logic errors or incorrect downstream behavior
findings.fix: Replace status: String, is_validated: bool, and is_sent: bool with a SessionStatus enum (e.g., Pending, Validated, Sent) and a SentMetadata struct carrying sent_at_epoch_ms. Remove is_sent entirely as it is redundant with the Sent variant.

findings.problem: status is a bare String, allowing any arbitrary value (e.g., "sent", "SENT", "", "deleted") instead of a closed set of domain states
findings.failure_mode: Invalid or typos'd status strings silently enter the system; pattern matching on status requires exhaustive string comparison instead of compile-time exhaustive enum variants
findings.fix: Replace status: String with an enum: enum SessionStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent { metadata: SentMetadata } }. Use exhaustive match instead of string equality.

findings.problem: is_sent: bool is redundant with status when status is refactored to an enum with a Sent variant. Having both creates a consistency hazard: they can diverge (is_sent=true but status="pending")
findings.failure_mode: Code that checks is_sent may behave differently from code that checks status == "sent", leading to inconsistent control flow
findings.fix: Remove is_sent: bool. Derive the sent state from the enum variant. Keep sent_at_epoch_ms inside the Sent variant.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes SessionWorkflow by value and mutates it in place. The function has no typed error return, so it silently succeeds for all inputs including already-sent or unvalidated sessions
findings.failure_mode: State transitions are not enforced; mark_sent can be called on any session regardless of its prior state, violating the workflow invariant that only validated sessions should transition to sent
findings.fix: Change mark_sent to accept a validated-session type (e.g., SessionStatus::Validated) and return Result<SessionWorkflow, TransitionError>. Or restructure so the enum variant encodes which transitions are valid.

findings.problem: id: String is a bare String with no domain constraints, length limits, or format validation. The SessionWorkflow struct has no constructor to validate or parse the id
findings.failure_mode: Empty, malformed, or excessively long session IDs can enter the system without any validation, causing downstream failures or security issues
findings.fix: Introduce a newtype SessionId(String) or SessionId(Vec<u8>) with a fallible constructor that validates length/format. Use it in place of bare String.

findings.problem: "sent".to_string() allocates a new String on every call to mark_sent. While this is a minor allocation, the struct already stores a String for id, meaning every mutable operation on session creates at least one allocation
findings.failure_mode: In high-throughput paths this causes unnecessary heap allocations. More importantly, the enum-based refactor should encode the state without heap allocation (e.g., &'static str or enum discriminant)
findings.fix: After the enum refactor, SessionStatus variants should use no heap allocation for the status tag. The Sent variant can carry only the metadata (sent_at_epoch_ms) without a separate String tag.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent throughput
no profiler data for allocation hot paths
no allocation tracking evidence for SessionWorkflow lifetime
no command-line or second-ring validation evidence
no CLI/subcommand surface or command-layer evidence
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate has no tests, no benchmarks, and no proof artifacts. The core domain model violation (primitive obsession with redundant booleans and String status) is the dominant risk — the code compiles but cannot enforce its own invariants. A refactored enum/typestate model must be verified with behavior tests before re-review.
